previous_support.label: Oct 6
previous_support.decision: Owner-approved continuity support: five continuous miles October 13, visibly conditional threshold October 15 and easy October 17. Keep October 8 easy and October 20 conditional. Six continuous miles remains the latest completed rung.
previous_support.mindset: He said he still thinks about Brice’s cue, “Stop negotiating with yourself.” The cue is about appropriate effort and reengagement, not overriding pain or a needed training change.
previous_support.engagement: José responded positively to the revision and called the continuous threshold a new challenge. This is engagement evidence, not readiness; the recovery gate remains explicit.

latest_jose_completion.athlete_response: Initially called the four miles easy; clarified 7/10 effort, breathing controlled, consciously restrained speed and slowed after watch average reached about 6:46/mi. Warm-up sluggish after prior-day leg strength.
latest_jose_completion.coach_read: Four miles at prescribed goal pace with deliberate restraint, RPE 7/10. Encouraging pacing execution, not a 4/10 easy effort or proof of lower physiological cost versus longer Oct 20 work.
latest_jose_completion.next_test: Nov 10 four-mile comparison and Nov 7/14 late-long-run goal-pace rehearsals. Capture mile splits, recovery and strength load.

pace_psychology.hypothesis: José reports running with others improves perceived ability to maintain rhythm; it is not causal proof.
pace_psychology.outcome: Oct 20: eight continuous miles at 6:44/mi felt hard. Oct 27: four at 6:48/mi, 7/10 effort with deliberate restraint and no breath limitation. Different doses; no causal conclusion.
pace_psychology.next_tests: Nov 10 four-mile goal-pace repeat; Nov 7 final three late; Nov 14 final five late with last two alongside steady company.
pace_psychology.race_strategy: Controlled opening around 6:50–6:51, even miles through nine, group for steadiness rather than a compulsory faster finish.
pace_psychology.measurement: Pace, RPE, company, reliable HR when comparable, fueling, weather, sleep, 24- and 48-hour recovery.

late_run_durability.fresh_test: Oct 27: first four-mile goal-pace work at 6:48/mi, 7/10 effort, breathing comfortable and pace restrained; warm-up slow after leg strength. Nov 10 repeat at 6:48–6:52/mi.
late_run_durability.taper: Nov 21 ten easy; Nov 28 eight easy; no third late-fast long run
late_run_durability.measures: Final 3/5 pace splits and steadiness; RPE entering the goal block, midway and at finish; comparable HR as context only; maple syrup and bottle quantities/tolerance; solo-to-partner transition; next-day and 48h recovery. Not a literal simulation of the last five miles after nine miles at race pace.
